- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts start above 80–90, while true values often dip below 80).
- Forecasts show upward drift or plateauing, but true outcomes frequently exhibit sharp downward corrections or mean reversion after spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >90), model tends to overcorrect or overshoot, then gradually decay — but true values often drop more abruptly or show volatility.
- Forecasts lag behind true values in the first 5–10 days, then gradually catch up — suggesting model is slow to react to short-term volatility.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 2023-05), model underestimates downward swings and overestimates upward ones, especially when true values show sharp drops after peaks.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 30-day horizon — often assumes continuation of trend, while true values revert to lower levels after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly smooth and lack volatility clustering — true outcomes show more frequent and sharper swings, especially in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon, then underestimates later days — suggesting a bias toward early overestimation.
- In cases where true values show a strong downward trend (e.g., 2023-05), model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly enough — leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model does not account for seasonal or event-driven volatility — true outcomes often show spikes or drops tied to external factors (e.g., policy, weather, market sentiment) not captured in baseline forecasts.
